item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. In 2024 Tshisekedi’s record looks more like crisis-era macro stabilization plus extractive revenue dependence than a serious effort to build broad-based, sustainable prosperity. I found some real positive signals on fiscal discipline, revenue mobilization, and stabilization, but they were narrow and often offset by opaque spending, weak social progress, and signs of resource squandering.

**Accepted Claims**
- [IMF Executive Board Concludes the 2024 Article IV Consultation and Completes the Sixth Review under the ECF Arrangement for the DRC](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr) | IMF | 2024-07-03 | The IMF said the authorities kept prudent macroeconomic policies, avoided monetary financing, and made some progress on domestic revenue mobilization. But it also said reform progress was slow, social and PFM reforms lagged, and the 2024 deficit would be narrowed largely because higher mining revenue offset security spending. This is the strongest positive evidence for prosperity intent, but it is still stability-first rather than broad-based transformation. | 5B.1, 4B.4, 4B.10

- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Congo, Democratic Republic of : April 2024 - Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099434404082425237) | World Bank | 2024-04-03 | The World Bank said growth prospects were favorable, but living conditions would not improve without much more ambitious reforms; it also flagged deficits, inflation, and downside risks. This suggests the economy was still not on a broad-based, sustainable prosperity path in 2024. | 5B.1

- [Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts - report](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-45741663/) | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | Reuters reported that CENI could not account for about $400 million and had awarded opaque contracts ahead of the election. That is direct evidence of rent-prone, non-transparent resource use, which cuts against a prosperity-building motive. | 5B.1, 4B.4, 4B.8

- [DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said Tshisekedi had made little to no progress on earlier pledges, that public resources were being squandered, and that essential social services were underfunded as a result. It also said mining expansion was driving forced evictions and pollution. This is strong negative evidence against broad-based, sustainable prosperity. | 5B.1, 4B.7, 4B.10, 4B.4

- [DRC: human rights priorities for the government during Tshisekedi’s second term](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr62/8155/2024/en/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty’s assessment is that the first term produced little progress and that the new term began with shrinking civic space, socioeconomic injustice, and weak resource management. It is a broad negative indicator that the administration had not shifted toward inclusive prosperity. | 5B.1, 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.4

- [Programme de desarmement et demobilisation, une alternative pour la paix et la cohesion sociale](https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-demobilisation-une-alternative-pour-la-paix-et-la-cohesion-sociale/) | ACP | 2024-03-22 | The government framed P-DDRCS as a stabilization, peace, and cohesion program meant to restore state authority where absent. That is limited positive evidence for creating the security conditions needed for durable prosperity, but it is indirect and not a substitute for a real development strategy. | 5B.1, 4B.7, 4B.10

- [Congo’s Tshisekedi fights poll fraud accusations with 'spirit of openness'](https://au.investing.com/news/commodities-news/congos-tshisekedi-fights-poll-fraud-accusations-with-spirit-of-openness-3074271) | Reuters | 2024-01-01 | Tshisekedi publicly said he would be a leader for all Congolese after the disputed election. This is weak positive rhetoric for inclusive governance, but it is thin evidence compared with the year’s stronger rent-seeking and underdelivery signals. | 5B.1, 4B.10

**Search Gap**
I did not find strong direct evidence of a coherent 2024 strategy to convert Congo’s mineral wealth into broad-based, sustainable prosperity. The best positive evidence is macro-stability and some reform talk; the best negative evidence is opaque public spending, weak social results, and resource-squandering / extractive-enclave dynamics.
